pearls.text: A wide QRS that does not meet criteria for left or right bundle branch block should be called an IVCD (intraventricular conduction delay).
pearls.verbatim: IVCD. Darn right. K. This is an IVCD.

pearls.text: When interpreting an EKG, look for T wave inversions in leads I, II, V5, and V6, not in V2-V3 where they can be a normal variant.
pearls.verbatim: Where should you be looking for T wave inversions, Doctor. Paul? Okay. Doctor. Page, tell us. One and two and v five and v six. That's right. Here and here. Right? Do you guys remember now? These two fingers right like that?

pearls.text: In atrial fibrillation with RVR, if the blood pressure is low (e.g., <100 systolic), giving rate control agents like metoprolol or diltiazem can cause further hypotension, which is preventable.
pearls.verbatim: It's because 90 over 60. Right? So you give them metoprolol or you give them Cardizem. What's gonna happen to that blood pressure? It'll come down. K? So then your next gene's gonna be 86 over whatever or 84 over whatever. Are you cool with that? No. What's more is that it was preventable.

pearls.text: When a patient with no known medical history presents with progressive shortness of breath, hypoxemia, and edema, frame the presentation as new-onset decompensated heart failure until proven otherwise.
pearls.verbatim: what is this patient's most likely diagnosis based on this presentation? Shout it out, everyone. Yes. Exactly. Okay? You guys are very noncommittal with that. One more time. Shout it out loud. Okay? Because heart failure. Yeah. Exactly.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: patients with no known medical history presenting with dyspnea, hypoxemia, and edema

pearls.text: Bradycardia is defined as heart rate less than 60 beats per minute.
pearls.verbatim: Less than 60 is bradycardia.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Lee Morning Report 9/10/26

pearls.text: When the diagnosis is uncertain, tell patients and families: 'We're not quite sure what's going on. I don't want to assume.'
pearls.verbatim: we're not quite sure what's going on. I just really don't wanna assume what's going on. And we all know what happens when we assume.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: If pneumonia was brewing prior to admission, classify it as community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) even if diagnosed after 48 hours in the hospital.
pearls.verbatim: I called out cap rather than half because despite the fact that I'm making the diagnosis greater than forty eight hours after admission, I think this was brewing prior to admission.

pearls.text: Chest pain should be asked about in patients with bilateral arm pain, as this might be the only way they present.
pearls.verbatim: Chest pain. Yes. Chest pain. Right? Yes. Good. This might be the only way they present.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Lee on Morning Report

pearls.text: Severe bilateral arm pain with confirmed platelets of 5 warrants immediate transfer to the ER, not dismissal as lab error.

pearls.text: A CT abdomen/pelvis delivers about 10 rads; the threshold for fetal harm is about 50 rads, so a single CT is safe if clinically indicated.
pearls.verbatim: A CT abdomen pelvis is about 10 radons. ... Fifty is about the cutoff for causing issues for for babies.

pearls.text: Appendicitis symptoms in early pregnancy are identical to the non-pregnant state; right lower quadrant pain remains consistent throughout pregnancy.

pearls.text: Round ligament pain typically occurs at the end of the second trimester/beginning of the third; it is a dull ache or sharp pulling sensation in the lower abdomen and groin.

pearls.text: Lightning crotch is a sudden, sharp, nerve-type pain in the groin radiating down the inner thigh or vagina, typically in the third trimester; its physiology is unknown.
pearls.verbatim: It's often in the third trimester. ... It's usually a sudden sudden sharp pain. It's intense. It originates in the groin and radiated down the inner thigh. Or sometimes people just say, like, it feels like it goes into my vagina.

pearls.text: ACOG states that in the absence of medical contraindication, maternal request alone is sufficient indication for pain relief during labor.

pearls.text: Neuraxial anesthesia should be offered for pain relief during any stage of labor, including early labor.

pearls.text: IV opioids (e.g., fentanyl) have little effect on maternal pain scores, provide unreliable analgesia, and cross the placenta with adverse neonatal effects including respiratory depression.

pearls.text: Trauma patients are at high risk for hypothermia because they are undressed and left uncovered during resuscitation; remember to cover them back up to prevent coagulopathy.
pearls.verbatim: it's forgotten to cover them back up. And so even though we keep... Probably they're hot, like, they're supposed to be that way to avoid the hypothermia, but they are still very at risk, which can cause coagulopathies

pearls.text: Loss of shivering is the hallmark of stage 3 hypothermia (core temperature 28-24°C).
pearls.verbatim: Stage three is now our 28 to 24 degrees Celsius, so very cold, and we're not shivering anymore. So that's kind of the hallmark for stage three.

pearls.text: Osborn waves on EKG are a deflection after the QRS complex; their height correlates with the degree of hypothermia and they are seen in stages 2 and 3.
pearls.verbatim: the height of that j wave or Osborn wave is related to the degree of hypothermia.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Nicole Tipton on Environmental Exposures 11/20/25

pearls.text: Fourth degree frostbite involves tendons, bones, and muscles; patients may have no sensation distally but still have pain proximally due to injury progression.
pearls.verbatim: by the time you get to fourth degree, you have involvement of everything deeper than the skin. So tendons, bones, muscles. ... They may not have sensation to those areas anymore, but they also may still be complaining of pain.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Nicole Tipton on Environmental Exposures 11/20/25

pearls.text: First step in hypothermia management is removing wet clothing and using passive external rewarming (bear hugger or warm blankets).
pearls.verbatim: If their wet clothes just sit on them, they're going to continue to lose body heat, and your rewarming efforts are going to be negated by that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Nicole Tipton
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Nicole Tipton on Environmental Exposures 11/20/25

pearls.text: When undressing a hypothermic patient, communicate with them, preserve modesty with a gown, and consider providing replacement clothing, especially for homeless patients who may be distressed about losing their clothes.

pearls.applies_to: patients requiring rapid undressing for hypothermia
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Nicole Tipton on Environmental Exposures 11/20/25

pearls.text: Warmed IV fluids raise core temperature by 0.5°C per hour; gastric lavage raises it by about 3°C per hour.
pearls.verbatim: warmed IV fluid is point five degrees Celsius. So we're not moving a ton. Right? ... gastric lavage, I think, was three degrees Celsius per hour.

pearls.applies_to: patients with moderate to severe hypothermia

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Nicole Tipton on Environmental Exposures 11/20/25

pearls.text: Rewarm frostbite in a 37, 39°C circulating water bath (e.g., sink with running water and temperature probe). Dry rewarming can be harmful.
pearls.verbatim: you have a thermal regulated water bath between 37 to 39 degrees Celsius. ... Dry rewarming is actually... Could be more harmful.

pearls.text: For heat edema, compression socks are helpful; diuretics are not helpful and can worsen dehydration.

pearls.text: Avoid using 'unresponsive' as it is nondescriptive; use specific terms like lethargic, stuporous, obtunded, or comatose.

pearls.verbatim: Very few of us do this in the clinic. It would be worth doing that from time to time. It is the thing that is studied and has better outcome data than BMI.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Sugar in food likely hijacks the dopamine axis, driving craving for more sugar.
pearls.verbatim: Sugar is put in everything because it probably hijacks your dopamine axis and makes you wanna go for more sugar.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Obesity rates are about 80% in disabled populations such as Down syndrome and cerebral palsy.
pearls.verbatim: Obesity rates are, like, eighty percent in that population.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Diabetes starts at a fasting glucose of 5.6; by 6.0 the horse is out of the barn, the patient is already metabolically sick.
pearls.verbatim: Diabetes starts at, like, five point six. ... someone comes in and they're obese and they're six, they're already at... The horse is out of the barn.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Triglycerides track very closely with sugar.
pearls.verbatim: Triglycerides track very closely with sugar.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Ask permission before discussing weight with a patient; do not assume their current weight is their heaviest.
pearls.verbatim: when they come to the doctor to just talk about it. Okay. But ask permission.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Document three numbers in the chart: heaviest weight, lightest weight, and goal weight.
pearls.verbatim: What's... You know, when when were you the heaviest? When were you the lightest? And then what's your goal? So where do you wanna be? And I write those three numbers down. I put them in the chart. Heaviest, lightest, goal.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Target 5-10% weight loss initially; 10% loss is a common goal (e.g., 22 pounds for a 220-pound patient).
pearls.verbatim: The 220 pounds was 10% loss. 22. 22. That's 10% loss. What's 5% loss? Half of that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Rapid weight loss (e.g., 20 pounds in 3 months) often leads to yo-yo rebound with higher weight and worse body composition.
pearls.verbatim: And then it's happened every single time that I've seen a patient that's done that. They yo yo right back up, and often it's higher. And their body composition is now worse.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Weight Watchers yields about 10% weight loss on average, which is enough to move many patients from BMI 28 to 25.
pearls.verbatim: on average, you're gonna get about 10%. That's about all you need for a lot of folks to get them a need. Right. To to get from whatever I was twenty twenty eight to 25.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Counseling is foundational; group counseling is more effective than individual.
pearls.verbatim: Group is better than the individual. Apps.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Group counseling is better than individual counseling for weight loss.
pearls.verbatim: Group is better than the individual.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Patients cannot exercise themselves to a healthy BMI from BMI 30-32; diet is 80% of initial weight loss.
pearls.verbatim: People cannot exercise themselves into a healthy BMI. They cannot do it. If they're a BMI of thirty, thirty two, they cannot exercise enough to get that down to a normal, right, a normal level. They have to be diet, behavioral changes, probably medication
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Sleeve gastrectomy is a 2-hour procedure, 2 days in hospital, 2 weeks recovery.
pearls.verbatim: I use the rule of twos when I talk to patients about it. It's a two hour procedure. You're in the hospital for two days, and you recover for two weeks on average.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Phentermine is a safe stimulant appetite suppressant, similar to Adderall; it was unfairly dragged down by fenfluramine's cardiac valve issues.
pearls.verbatim: It's a very safe medication. You guys write people that so much more dangerous than phentermine. And every day you're doing this. Who's for Adderall? Who's writing for Ritalin? These are these are stimulants. Guess what? That's the same class of drugs as phentermine.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Qsymia (phentermine/topiramate) can be created cheaply from generics; the brand is expensive at a couple bucks a pill.
pearls.verbatim: Qsymia is, like, a couple bucks a pill. Dang. Very expensive. Phentermine topiramate by itself is like pennies.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Bupropion/naltrexone works best for patients with addictive or behavioral eating phenotypes.
pearls.verbatim: Bupropion, naltrexone, this is for your people that have kind of that almost addictive kind of eating or behavioral kind of eating, that phenotype. Works a little bit better.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: adults with obesity and addictive/behavioral eating
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Xenical (orlistat) causes oily incontinence if patients eat a high-fat meal; one episode ends patient trust.
pearls.verbatim: Your patients, if you write them for Xenical and you don't tell them to eat a low fat meal It leaks. They will think they're gonna pass a little gas, and it's not gas. Now I'm going to the bathroom to change my pants, and it only has to happen one time. Never trust you or that drug again.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: GLP-1s cause loss of lean muscle mass; patients need high protein intake (1 gram per pound of body weight if kidneys normal) and resistance training focusing on large muscles (squats, deadlifts).
pearls.verbatim: This is a very high level of protein intake. One gram a pound is a ton of protein. If they're normal, they have normal kidneys, they can do it. You gotta get there. They're... They are gonna start wasting away. So cut servings in half, start fiber, start resistance training. That's what I tell them all. What do I mean by resistance training? Your butt and your thighs is the big muscles in your body. I'm not talking about the little... That's what all the guys wanna do is the biceps. Right? Know it's squats and deadlift and, like, big muscles because that's what you... That's where you need the mass.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: adults on GLP-1 agonists with normal kidney function
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Mounjaro is only FDA-approved for diabetes; prescribing it for obesity will be denied by insurance.
pearls.verbatim: It is only FDA approved for diabetes. Don't try to send it in for obesity. It will be denied every time.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Once at goal weight, back off the GLP-1 dose to the lowest effective dose for cost; it takes a long time for weight to return, and you can extend intervals to every 10-14 days.
pearls.verbatim: Once they're a goal weight, I start talking about backing them off. It it takes a long time for them to start gaining their weight back, and so you'll know, oh, we're starting to eat a lot more. Well, maybe we should go back. So every ten days, even every fourteen days.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: patients at goal weight on GLP-1 agonists
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: GLP-1 agonists carry warnings for history of pancreatitis, multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome, and thyroid cancer.
pearls.verbatim: And the GLP ones, and this one is true, history of pancreatitis or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome, and then thyroid cancer.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Topamax (topiramate) is good for patients who get up and eat at night; it causes taste disturbance that reduces desire for sweets.
pearls.verbatim: CopaMax, I like at nighttime. This is really good for people who get up and eat at night, and and it gives you a little taste disturbance. And so a lot of those... A lot of my patients actually like that because they don't wanna eat sweets.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: When sending a clearance form to the surgeon, also write and attach a formal report listing the patient's specific risks; this distinguishes you from most primary care physicians.
pearls.verbatim: I have a report that I print off for every patient that I do this for. I send that plus the little form they asked for to them. When you do that, you're doing better than every primary care physician in town.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Recognize spiritual risks before surgery: assess the patient's hope, fear, anxiety, and beliefs about God's will or illness causation, as these are often overlooked resources or vulnerabilities.
pearls.verbatim: What are the spiritual risks associated with this surgery? ... How afraid are you? Why are you afraid? Where is the fear coming from? Where is the anxiety coming from? Is it God's will that you're having this surgery or not? Is the devil making you sick?
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Most patients go into elective surgery in a sub-optimized nutritional state, either overweight or underweight, which impairs recovery.
pearls.verbatim: Turns out that most of our patients are going into surgery, even elective surgery, in a sub optimized nutritional state. Either they're big, they're skinny, skinny.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Assess social support structure before surgery; patients without family or caregivers and from depressed socioeconomic situations have worse outcomes.
pearls.verbatim: They show that when families... When patients come from either a depressed socioeconomic situation where they don't have family, they don't have caregivers, they might be... They have really bad outcomes.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Nutritional risk factors include BMI less than 21 and age over 65; protein malnutrition is the most predictive of bad outcomes.
pearls.verbatim: BMI less than twenty one, age over 65, that's every hip fracture that you have seen in the ER. Right? So that's really important. If you're in a nursing home, these are these are people who are, by definition, usually nutritionally depressed. So they're gonna be protein malnourished, which is the most predictive bad outcome.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: elderly patients, especially those with hip fracture or from nursing homes
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: For patients over 65 having major surgery, most pre-op physicians would get a CBC; the value is in finding incidental anemia, not in assessing pre-op risk.
pearls.verbatim: Pretty much everyone 65 that's having major surgery will get an H and H. But it's usually in the form of a CBC. The white count is not usually helpful. The platelets are occasionally helpful if you're gonna do some kind of spinal anesthesia. So over 65, most pre-op physicians would say should get a CBC. It's not because of the pre-op risk. It's because of the low hanging fruit of finding something else in that age category.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: For patients over 65 having major surgery, most pre-op physicians recommend a CBC, not for pre-op risk but to find incidental findings.
pearls.verbatim: So over 65, most pre-op physicians would say should get a CBC. It's not because of the pre-op risk. It's because of the low hanging fruit of finding something else in that age category.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: For a 35-year-old, the chance of finding something on a CBC is almost zero, and the chance of finding something you didn't want to know is higher than zero, so routine CBC is not indicated.
pearls.verbatim: As a 35 year old, your chance of finding something else is, like, almost zero, as close to zero as you can get. And your chance of finding something you didn't wanna know is higher than zero.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: When you involve a cardiologist for pre-op clearance, you will often get a letter back saying 'no further testing required', they rarely order extensive testing.
pearls.verbatim: So when you involve a cardiologist, like, a lot of times, if you just feel a little bit itchy and, the patient, I just don't really feel comfortable. This guy's got congestive failure. I would... I'd like him to see a cardiologist. It's amazing. You will get a a letter back that just says no further testing required.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: patients with known congestive heart failure referred to cardiology
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: A good exercise MPS pushes patients to about 10 METs; if they can survive that, they will likely tolerate surgery.
pearls.verbatim: How many METs is an MPS? When you do the exercise MPS, how many METs are they pushing those patients? About 10. So good MPS is 10. And if they can do an MPS and survive, they're gonna be okay doing their surgery.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: patients undergoing cardiac stress testing before surgery
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: If a patient's A1c is 12, delay surgery and work with them monthly until glucose control improves before re-referring to the surgeon.
pearls.verbatim: A common one is diabetes. So if they come in and their A1c is 12, kind of a no brainer. You'll see them maybe monthly or every couple weeks to a month as they're getting better and better. Then, hey. Why don't you reach out to your surgeon? Looks like things are going in the right direction.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: A positive anti-HCV antibody with a positive HCV RNA test indicates current infection; a negative RNA with positive antibody suggests past infection.
pearls.verbatim: RNA is kind of the gold standard. Right? If it's present, if RNA... HCV RNA is present, they have an infection regardless of their antibody status.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: adults being tested for hepatitis C
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Family medicine should manage hepatitis C in the clinic, as many patients are not receiving care and it is not a difficult process for most patients.
pearls.verbatim: We have a population of folks with hep C that are coming in all the time, and we're not treating them. We're going to other places.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: About 75% of people with chronic hepatitis C are unaware of their infection, highlighting the need for universal screening.
pearls.verbatim: about seventy five percent of those are unaware that they have the infection.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Deaths from hepatitis C now exceed deaths from HIV, primarily due to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
pearls.verbatim: we still see deaths from hepatitis C now higher than deaths from HIV.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Hepatitis C is curable with direct-acting antivirals, achieving over 90% sustained virologic response.
pearls.verbatim: we came up with a with a medication, a set of medications that causes a cure in over ninety percent sustained virologic response.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Baby boomers (born 1945-1965) account for about 75% of hepatitis C cases in the US, but universal screening for all adults 18 and older is now recommended.
pearls.verbatim: baby boomers actually now account for about seventy five percent or more of the of the hepatitis C in The US.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: HCV RNA determines active replicating virus; antibody alone cannot distinguish past cleared infection from current viremia, so you need the cascade test.
pearls.verbatim: The HCV RNA is what determines whether you have active replicating virus in your body. People who have cleared this virus and anywhere from five to fifteen, twenty percent folks in some studies will actually clear this virus and not have chronic viremia. That's this. They will have antibody often of their RNAs as zero, which is why you want that cascade. You can't make the decision based on just antibody.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: patients with positive hepatitis C antibody
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Home hepatitis C test kits are FDA-approved and available over the counter for about $75; patients may present with positive results from these tests.
pearls.verbatim: about $75, you can buy this over the counter, and you can have a mail in. Anybody, yes, comes back in a few weeks. These are FDA approved. Five of them on the market now. So I've had a couple patients come in with the home test as positive.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Over 90% of otherwise healthy patients with hepatitis C (no chronic alcoholism, terrible diabetes, etc.) will have zero fibrosis on workup.
pearls.verbatim: if they're otherwise healthy and they're not, you know, chronic alcoholics, terrible diabetes, you know, whatever. I mean, if they're not really, really sick people, they're gonna do all of these tests, and they're gonna come back zero fibrosis, probably ninety plus percent of the time.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: otherwise healthy adults with hepatitis C
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: For simplified treatment, the patient must have chronic hepatitis C (any genotype), no cirrhosis, and no prior treatment; these patients can be managed in primary care.
pearls.verbatim: Who is eligible for simplified treatment? Chronic hepatitis C, any genotype, did not have cirrhosis, and have not been treated. That's like everybody. Right? That's everybody who comes in almost.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: adults with newly diagnosed hepatitis C
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Patients with prior treatment failure, cirrhosis, hepatitis B coinfection, pregnancy, suspected hepatocellular carcinoma, or transplant should be referred to a hepatologist or ID specialist.
pearls.verbatim: These are people that I would refer out to a hepatologist who... Or to an ID. These are people who've been treated before that have cirrhosis. Although there's... You can do some of this solo if you're careful with cirrhosis, if they've got hepatitis B, obviously, if they're pregnant, or if you think they have carcinoma or it's a transplant.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: The two main treatment regimens are Mavyret (3 pills daily for 8 weeks) and Epclusa (1 pill daily for 12 weeks); no lab monitoring is required during therapy.
pearls.verbatim: Two drugs, you guys. This is it. Mavarette, Zipclusa Easy. I mean, like, you do a lot more complicated things than this in your practice. So three pills for eight weeks. This is. This is Epclusa one pill a day for twelve weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: adults with hepatitis C eligible for simplified treatment
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Epclusa is given as one pill daily for twelve weeks for HCV.
pearls.verbatim: one pill a day for twelve weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Bring HCV patients in once a month during treatment to check on them.
pearls.verbatim: While they're on it, you bring them in once a month, something like that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: After completing HCV treatment, check a viral RNA at twelve weeks.
pearls.verbatim: Post treatment, you wanna do a viral RNA at twelve weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: patients who have completed HCV treatment
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Noncirrhotic patients who achieve sustained virologic response need no liver-related follow-up.
pearls.verbatim: No liver related follow-up is recommended for noncirrhotic patients who achieve sustained virologic response.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Watch for hypoglycemia as a side effect of HCV treatment, especially in diabetics.
pearls.verbatim: The biggest side effect has to do with the hypoglycemia question I've seen. I've had that in my clinic, but one of them was a diabetic.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.applies_to: patients on HCV treatment, especially diabetics
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Educate patients about the importance of committing to the full HCV treatment course.
pearls.verbatim: I mean, this does take quite a bit of education. You really do need to let them know, hey. This is, you know, this is a big deal. I want you to commit to this three month, two month, three month process,
pearls.speaker: Dr. Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place Outpatient Lecture

pearls.text: Advise caution with extreme sports like CrossFit, as the heavy lifting and pounding put excessive pressure on the pelvic floor that the body was not made to handle.
pearls.verbatim: I really do not encourage patients to do CrossFit. The body was just not made to be under that kind of extreme pressure when they're crunching or trying to lift those 100 bell weights, the pelvic floor is just not made for it.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Tell patients to imagine clenching their butt cheeks in a room full of people and trying not to pass gas to perform a proper Kegel exercise.
pearls.verbatim: imagine yourself trying to clench your butt cheeks in a room full of people and not trying to pass gas.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: To test Kegel strength, have the patient try to stop urine midstream once a month, but not more often to avoid causing voiding dysfunction.
pearls.verbatim: try to do that midstream peeing and see if you can stop yourself peeing. If so, you've done a good Kegel. Don't try to do it and create, like, avoiding dysfunction. We don't want you to do that every time you pee. Do it, like, once a month or so to see how strong your Kegels are.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: For patients with diabetes and incontinence, first get their blood sugar under control with a hemoglobin A1c under 7% before addressing the urinary issues.
pearls.verbatim: we always want their hemoglobin a one c to be under 7%. But when they have that excess sugar, then it goes all under urine, and they have polyuria.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Do not assume every woman knows there are three separate openings (urethra, vagina, rectum) or knows how to do a Kegel; educating patients on anatomy is important.
pearls.verbatim: Everyone makes the assumption that every woman knows how to kegel or every woman knows there's three holes down there. Do not make that assumption.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Urinary incontinence is not a normal part of aging; one in four women aged 20-39 also suffers from it, so it should be asked about in younger women as well.
pearls.verbatim: one in four women aged 20 to 39 will suffer from urinary incontinence.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Nocturia is defined as waking up more than two times during the night to urinate, though the definition is patient-centered based on increased bother.
pearls.verbatim: if you're waking up more than two times during the night, you're probably having nocturia.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Advise patients to avoid the four C's: carbonated drinks, citrusy things, caffeinated drinks, and chocolate, as these are high in acid and irritate the bladder lining, causing urgency and frequency.
pearls.verbatim: avoid the four c's. Carbonated drinks, citrusy things, caffeinated drinks, and chocolate.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Teach Kegels as a set of 10, each held for 10 seconds, twice daily.
pearls.verbatim: we tell them pretty much to do a set of 10 and hold it for ten seconds. So when they're squeezing, try to hold it for ten seconds and do a set of 10 and try to do that twice a day.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: PTNS protocol: 25-minute sessions weekly for 12 weeks, then maintenance every 4, 6 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: they get stimulation right by their ankle, the tibial nerve, for about twenty five minutes one time a week for about twelve weeks, and then they come for maintenance therapy once every four to six weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.applies_to: patients with overactive bladder interested in non-drug therapy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Bladder Botox wears off after 6, 12 months, requiring injections once or twice a year.
pearls.verbatim: Botox will blow off eventually between six, twelve months because they get injection once to twice a year.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.applies_to: patients receiving bladder Botox for overactive bladder
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: In elderly patients, if an anticholinergic is needed, choose trospium (Sanctura) because it is a quaternary amine and does not cross the blood-brain barrier, minimizing cognitive effects.
pearls.verbatim: If you have to do an anticholinergic, it's Trospium.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: A pessary acts like a speed bump under the urethra, preventing leakage with cough, laugh, or sneeze.
pearls.verbatim: The knob actually rests right under the pee hole, and think of it like a speed bump so that when you cough, flap, and sneeze, you don't leave.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: Tell patients the pessary should feel like a tampon, noticeable at first, then forgotten.
pearls.verbatim: I always tell patients, it should feel like a tampon. You know it's there. But then after a while, you don't know it's there.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: For young, healthy patients, clean the pessary once a week with warm soap and water, let it dry overnight, and reinsert the next morning.
pearls.verbatim: if they're young and healthy, I usually tell them clean your pessary once a week. Right? So on Sunday, wash it with warm soap and water, put it on the nightstand overnight to dry, and then on Monday morning, put it back in.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price
pearls.applies_to: young, healthy patients using a pessary
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Price on Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

pearls.text: The more patients wash and dry the pessary, the less vaginal discharge they will have.
pearls.verbatim: The more that they wash and clean it and let it dry, the less vaginal discharge they'll have.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Price

pearls.speaker: Dr. Richard

pearls.text: Disc pain presents with localized back pain, not radicular pain, and on exam you find isolated paraspinal spasms at the level of the disc.
pearls.verbatim: So the disc itself has got sensation, got a capsule. Gonna have a rupture in that capsule, gonna have a bulge. It's gonna hurt, and it's gonna make the back feel like there's a problem. So there's going to be localized back pain, but not radicular pain.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: On physical exam for disc pain, look for isolated paraspinal spasms at the level of the pain, which indicates the disc level to target on MRI.
pearls.verbatim: So you have paraspinal spasms surrounding the area of the disc to try to splint that naturally. Right? So that's what you're looking for on your physical exam is isolated paraspinal spasms at the level of the pain where the disc problem is, and then you know where to look on your MRI scan to see that there's a problem with that disc.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: Facet joint pain is worse with extension, lateralized to one side of the spine, and significantly better when lying down; it does not produce radicular leg pain.

pearls.applies_to: patients with chronic low back pain
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: Neurogenic claudication pain is typically symmetrical and affects the upper legs first, then moves down to the lower legs and feet.
pearls.verbatim: So that radicular pain or that claudication pain generally is symmetrical, and it's usually upper parts of the legs rather than being a line right down the leg and into the foot like a truadicular pain stuff.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: Omega-3 supplements (vegan-based, 2 capsules three times daily, targeting ~1500 mg total) have a significant anti-inflammatory effect and are very safe for back pain, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoarthritis.
pearls.verbatim: The vegan omega threes are very cheap. You can get them on Amazon, and they have a fairly profound anti inflammatory effect. And you just tell them get, you know, two capsules of of a vegan based omega three three times a day, and you will have enough of an anti inflammatory effect that you'll be able to tell a significant difference.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: Turmeric is less well-tolerated than omega-3 due to gastric irritation and staining; omega-3 has better evidence for anti-inflammatory effect.

Turmeric's big problem, you know, reason that PPIs are prescribed is everybody has gastritis from drinking coffee at Starbucks. Right? The turmeric has a very strong acidic component to it that irritates almost everybody's gastric mucosa, so it's hard to tolerate. And then it stains everything yellow.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: MRI is indicated when patients fail conservative therapy and interventional treatments are being considered.
pearls.verbatim: somewhere in this break point is where we're thinking about, yeah. Now it's time to get the MRI scan to confirm what I think is going on.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.applies_to: patients with persistent back pain failing conservative management
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.applies_to: patients with chronic low back pain
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: The hallmark of a spinal compression fracture is excruciating pain with rotation of the upper body relative to the lower body, not just spinous process tenderness.

pearls.text: Kyphoplasty by interventional radiology can provide dramatic pain relief for compression fractures; patients often express great gratitude.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain

pearls.text: Any fracture in a middle-aged or older patient should prompt evaluation for osteoporosis or low bone density, even if the mechanism seems traumatic.

pearls.text: The enteric nervous system has two plexuses: one controls peristalsis (myenteric), the other controls absorption through the mucous membrane.
pearls.verbatim: This is primary control of peristalsis. This is primary control of absorption through that mucous membrane.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Autoantibodies against the absorption-controlling plexus can cause both constipation and diarrhea in IBS.
pearls.verbatim: if you have antibodies that make the absorption controller not work, you can see why you can have constipation and diarrhea with irritable bowel syndrome.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Autoantibodies against the muscular control system (myenteric plexus) cause constipation, diarrhea, and cramping due to altered transit speed.
pearls.verbatim: If you have problems with antibodies against the muscular control system, then what's that gonna result in? Constipation diarrhea because of the speed of the movement through, but then also cramping.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Viruses can trigger autoantibodies because when they bud from host cells, the viral capsule contains host cell membrane proteins, making the immune system attack both virus and host cell.
pearls.verbatim: a virus goes into the cell. But then when it reproduces in the cell and comes out of it, that the cell wall is what makes up the capsule of the virus.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: A gluten-free diet is not more efficient than a low-fermentable diet for IBS; different diets each have their contribution.
pearls.verbatim: a gluten free diet is not more efficient than low fermentable. So the different diets all have their contribution correcting the problem that we're talking about.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Post-infectious IBS is a proven clinical entity with augmented cellular immune response and correlating immune cell counts.

pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: The mechanism of virus-induced autoimmunity is the same as in type 1 diabetes: coxsackievirus in pancreatic islet cells triggers antibodies that later destroy beta cells.
pearls.verbatim: It's the same way that type one diabetes develops when you have coxsackievirus in in the islet cells in the pancreas.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Inflammatory bowel disease is associated with a 20 times higher risk of psoriasis.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: In IBS, aim to normalize bowel function to one or two bowel movements per day using soluble fiber, probiotics, Miralax, and loperamide, customized to the patient.
pearls.verbatim: that you're striving to normalize the bowel experience. Right? If they're loose, you want them to be tighter. If they're tight, you want them to be looser. You want them to have a normal bowel movement once or twice a day.

pearls.applies_to: patients with IBS or chronic abdominal pain
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Long-term maintenance is required for IBS treatment; stopping therapy typically leads to symptom recurrence.
pearls.verbatim: I'm ready to stop taking all of these. No. If you stop taking all of these, it's gonna go right back the way it was before. You're not you're not fixing anything. You're normalizing what's going on with the bowel.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: For patients who fail low-FODMAP, a gluten-free diet may help even without celiac antibodies, possibly due to other immune mechanisms.

But then even the people that don't have that, for some reason, IgG and IgA are assayed, and they're not responding to the gluten IgG and IgA, but to other antibodies that are also better when they're gluten free.

pearls.applies_to: patients with IBS not responding to low-FODMAP diet

pearls.text: Allow 10-12 weeks for each dietary intervention to work, because antibody levels take 6-8 weeks to drop and inflammation takes about 4 weeks to settle.
pearls.verbatim: It takes about six or eight weeks for those levels to go down and then about four weeks for the the inflammation that has been caused by the antibodies that were there to settle down. So make changes that happen quicker than every ten weeks is not a... It's just not reasonable with the pathophysiology you're working with.

pearls.applies_to: patients undergoing dietary elimination for IBS
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: When a food antibody panel shows many positives, start by eliminating the highest-level reactions (e.g., class five) for twelve weeks, then reassess before removing more.

pearls.applies_to: patients with positive food antibody panels
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: Anti-inflammatory or antispasmodic agents, such as peppermint oil, can be effective for the symptomatology of chronic abdominal pain.
pearls.verbatim: So so anything that is an anti inflammatory or an antispasmodic is effective in the symptomatology that goes along with this.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: If patients do not get answers from IgG-guided elimination, refer them to an allergist for further testing.
pearls.verbatim: And then when you still have a group of people that aren't getting their answers, that's when you start to talk to the allergist about doing their testing.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.applies_to: patients with chronic abdominal pain unresponsive to IgG-guided elimination
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on Chronic Abdominal Pain

pearls.text: COPD is inflammation of the alveoli and basement membrane, not the larger airways.
pearls.verbatim: The basement membrane of the alveoli.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: In COPD, alveolar destruction and inflammation cause collapse and atelectasis, leading to dead space and air trapping.
pearls.verbatim: collapse and and causes atelectasis.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: Asthma involves both chronic inflammation (hypertrophied mucosa, eosinophils, mucus gland hyperplasia) and bronchial hyperreactivity, not just bronchospasm.
pearls.verbatim: So it's not just reactivity in asthma. It's inflammation and reactivity.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: To determine if a COPD patient has a reactive component, look for reversibility on spirometry with a bronchodilator challenge.
pearls.verbatim: Reversibility. See if they respond to a bronchodilator.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: If a PFT says no response to bronchodilators, there is no reason to use a bronchodilator in that patient.
pearls.verbatim: if it says no response to bronchodilators, is there an efficacy or a reason to use a bronchodilator in that patient? No. You shouldn't do that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: A COPD exacerbation requires a change in cough and a change in sputum production; change in sputum character is supportive but not required.
pearls.verbatim: It has to have change in cough. It has to have change in sputum production. It should have, doesn't have to, but it should have change in sputum character.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: The typical COPD exacerbation story evolves over weeks, not hours or overnight.
pearls.verbatim: it's never overnight. It's never hours. A COPD exacerbation, flavor of it is this is a prolonged story. I knew there was something going on a couple of weeks ago.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Rylander
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: If a patient cannot produce sputum but has two of the three cardinal features (change in cough, sputum production, sputum character), it can still be a COPD exacerbation.
pearls.verbatim: If they're not physically producing mucus, it's less likely to be a COPD exacerbation, but it's not an If they've got all the rest of that story and they've got two out of three, I'm okay with that.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.text: Heart failure exacerbations present more rapidly (hours to days) than COPD exacerbations, often triggered by dietary salt or medication changes.
pearls.verbatim: the script for congestive heart failure is much more rapid, much more fluid kind of dynamic change that happens, and it happens... That's what happens overnight. That's what happens in two or three days.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.verbatim: If you don't relax, it takes greater pressure... Filling pressure that people don't generate so you don't get a big load and get it out. Now your ejection fraction is preserved.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.verbatim: And it's a chemical reaction, the digestion, and the inflammation to that stuff being in there. And that can be sterile the whole time. You don't need antibiotics for pneumonitis. You need steroids.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Rylander on COPD and Asthma

pearls.verbatim: why you don't give somebody that's got RSV a albuterol inhaler and just say, oh, well, I don't need albuterol inhaler if, you know, you just got RSV.
