pearls.text: The NOVA classification system categorizes foods: class 1 unprocessed/minimally processed, class 2 processed culinary ingredients (butter, sugar, salt, oils), class 3 processed foods (typically three ingredients, e.g., canned green beans with sodium), and class 4 ultra-processed foods.
pearls.verbatim: Class one would be, like, unprocessed, minimally processed. Class two would be, like, processing culinary ingredients, like butter that you cook with. You don't usually eat these individually. Butter, sugar, salt, oils. Category three is processed foods, which is typically three ingredients. Like, for example, if you have, like, fresh green beans or frozen green beans, that would be, like, unprocessed or minimally processed. But if you can those green beans, like, in sodium to preserve it, has probably got three ingredients, that would be considered processed category three. And kinda category four is ultra processed foods.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Ultra-processed foods are defined as industrial formulations of processed food substances containing little or no whole foods, typically including flavorings, colorings, emulsifiers, and other additives.
pearls.verbatim: And how we define that is industrial formulations of processed food substances such as oil, solids, fats, etcetera, that contain little or no whole foods and typically include flavorings, colorings, emulsifiers, and other additives.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: 60% of the American diet comes from ultra-processed foods.
pearls.verbatim: 60% of their diet is from ultra processed foods.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Ultra-processed foods drive overconsumption through low cost, prolonged shelf life, hyperpalatability (fat/carb/sugar ratios), semi-solid texture allowing faster eating, high energy density, and digestive alterations.
pearls.verbatim: Food choice are typically lower cost. They're cheaper. They're more affordable. They're prolonged shelf life. They can last a long time in your pantry. The hyperpalatability part of it, the fat ratio, the carb ratio, the sugar ratios as well. Food texture. Usually, ultrafast foods are semi solid. You can eat them at a much, much quicker rate. I have study to show you on that as well. Energy density, digestive alterations as well.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Ultra-processed foods are engineered to have supernormal rewarding properties that may result in pathological eating behavior.
pearls.verbatim: Engineered to have supernormal repetitive properties, rewarding properties, that may result in pathological eating behavior,
pearls.speaker: Dr. Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Neurons in the GI tract sense glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids, and can trigger dopamine release even when sugar is not consciously tasted, leading to unconscious reward-driven eating.
pearls.verbatim: there are neurons in your GI tract that sense glucose, that sense amino acids, that sense fatty acids. So you can eat a food that doesn't even... And, like, because it's so salted and all all the other additives, don't really taste that there's sugar in there. But when you consume it, that sugar will get identified by those neurons that will release dopamine, and you will still, like, be getting that that reward pathway. Right? So there's... It's... So it's also unconscious as well.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: In a controlled metabolic study, participants on an ultra-processed diet ate about 500 more calories per day than those on a minimally processed diet, even when calories and macronutrients were matched.

pearls.text: When reading a nutrition label, if the % Daily Value for a nutrient is 5% or lower per serving, it is considered low in that nutrient; if 20% or higher, it is high.

pearls.text: Total sugar on a label includes both natural and added sugars; the added sugars line tells you how much is added. For example, if total sugar is 12g and added sugar is 10g, only 2g are natural.

pearls.text: When a patient presents with low libido, assess expectations, whether it has changed, and comorbid conditions before labeling it as a disorder.
pearls.verbatim: What are your expectations? Assessing expectations and whatever conversation that's happened with him or her partner is or past partners have been. And assess assess for other comorbid, you know, disorders.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Satterlee & Dr. Hildebrand
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Women tend to recognize a broad range of stimuli as sexually relevant, but then evaluate eagerness and enjoyment differently; this is not the same as thinking about sex more than men.
pearls.verbatim: So the research is... Would suggest that, actually, women see many things that's sexually relevant, but then they evaluate their eagerness differently, and enjoyment is different. K? So just important to not buy the myth that, like, and think about sex a lot more than women do. Actually, women think about sex in terms of, like... But they may quickly move on to something else. A lot of other things are in place.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Satterlee & Dr. Hildebrand
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Genital response (e.g., lubrication) is not a reliable indicator of subjective sexual arousal; concordance between genital and subjective arousal is only about 10-25% in women.
pearls.verbatim: Only 50% overlap consistently for men, maximum, and it's much less for women. Perhaps, like, 10 to 25. So what this suggests is, again, what the brain says is arousing and what the genitals say arousing are not always the same thing, which is one reason that the idea that female, for example, lubrication or wetness should be the determination of her arousal.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Satterlee & Dr. Hildebrand
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: The most common issue in behavioral medicine for women is not low libido but difficulty removing the brakes; common brake factors include stress, perception of not being cared for, low affection, and lack of explicitly erotic context.
pearls.verbatim: And break relief is actually the number one thing that we tend to work with women on in terms of behavioral med. It's very seldom actually low libido unless it's physiologically related to, like, an illness or to a medication. It's more about, can we help them get the brakes off? What are the things... They may have a less than sensitive gas pedal, but more likely, it's a brake problem. So what are some of the things to put brakes off on for women? Stress. Right? A perception of not being cared for, low affection, or things not being explicitly erotic.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Satterlee & Dr. Hildebrand
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Ischemic strokes receive IVF without dextrose if the patient is volume depleted, which most patients tend to be.
pearls.verbatim: Ischemic strokes, on the other hand, do receive IVF without dextrose specifically if a patient is volume depleted, which most patients tend to be.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: In ESRD patients on HD, cardiac morbidity and mortality risk is 25-40% higher on the first day after HD compared to any other day, due to volume overload and hyponatremia.
pearls.verbatim: Twenty five to forty percent higher risk of cardiac MIs or A-fib exacerbations or acute volume overload that worsens CHF on the first day of HD compared to any other day.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Volume overload in ESRD is primarily treated by dialysis; longer and more frequent HD sessions (e.g., q4 rather than q3) can help prevent it.
pearls.verbatim: main treatment for volume overload in ESRD is to dialyze them. More specific looks at how to dialyze patients to prevent volume overload and sodium overload over the course of the weekend is to have longer sessions and more frequent HD schedules during the week, so doing q four rather than q three
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Always check the MAR when assuming care of a patient from the night team to identify running IV fluids and other medications that may not be documented in notes.
pearls.verbatim: check the MAR every time that we are assuming care of a patient from the night team or we're coming on to FMIS onto a new month, making sure we know exactly what the patient's getting, what they're getting at, looking at RN meds, making sure we have fluids
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.applies_to: residents assuming care of a patient
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: When consulting specialists, check the MAR to see if they changed any orders, such as when nephrology discontinues IVF.
pearls.verbatim: when we're consulting specialists, so checking them are to make sure that any of our specialists changing things that we had ordered, like when nephro, DC, V, IVF have it on.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Document all treatments, especially IVF, in the H&P and progress notes under the specific problem it is treating or in the FEN section.
pearls.verbatim: documenting all treatments, especially IVF, a drug that's being added to the patient in our HNPs and in our progress notes under either the specific problem that it's treating or in an FEN section.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Atypical presentations of ACS, such as dyspnea without chest pain, are common and can lead to delays in care; maintain a high index of suspicion.
pearls.verbatim: the biggest thing is really the atypical presentation of this, and we'll go into, like, we'll go into that in a little bit of detail.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: To diagnose CHF, you need at least two major criteria: pulmonary edema, cardiomegaly, jugular reflex, PAN D, and third heart sound.
pearls.verbatim: You need at least two major criteria. So pulmonary edema, which actually has that as well. Cardioomegaly, jugular reflex.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: One third of patients with confirmed MI have no chest pain; dyspnea alone can be a presentation.
pearls.verbatim: Of the one third of patients with confirmed MI had no chest pain.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: In the ER, any patient over 50 with shortness of breath should get an EKG because of concern for MI.
pearls.verbatim: In the ER, anyone coming in with shortness of breath who's 50 years old, like, they're... That's why they get the EKG on almost everybody.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.applies_to: patients over 50 with dyspnea in the ER
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Shortness of breath should be nuanced like pain; don't forget it can be an anginal equivalent.
pearls.verbatim: my takeaway was shortness of breath, nuance it, view it like just pain. Like, don't forget that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: The most important cause of new heart failure is ischemic cardiac disease; maintain high suspicion even without chest pain.
pearls.verbatim: the most important cause of heart failure is ischemic cardiac disease, and so having a higher suspicion of that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Severe neutropenia is defined as an ANC less than 500; this patient had an ANC of 200.
pearls.verbatim: ANC was point two, so that's 200, and severe neutropenia is anything that's less than 500.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Risk stratification tools for febrile neutropenia (e.g., MASC index) are available on MD Calc to help guide management.
pearls.verbatim: This goes through some risk calculations for febrile neutropenia. They're all on MD calc, MASC, and the others you can plug in again and then these scores to kind of restratify them.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: In febrile neutropenia, antibiotic administration within 30 minutes lowers mortality compared to longer delays.
pearls.verbatim: timing to antibiotics less than thirty minutes to lower mortality than those greater than thirty minutes.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Direct admissions to the floor often result in delayed notification of the treating team; this is a systemic safety problem.
pearls.verbatim: direct admissions coming to the floor and then treating teams not being notified.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: File a variance for any issue that needs systemic change; verbal reports alone won't lead to policy changes, documentation is required.
pearls.verbatim: we got to file a variance to make any type of systemic change. Like, we can tell people all we want, but without it being documented.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Youmans & Dr. Wheeler & Dr. Jones
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Infant massage can help with drug-addicted babies, jaundice, postpartum depression, and failure to thrive.

pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Domestic violence patients can text a code word to the presenter, who will send police to their home if available.
pearls.verbatim: they will text me a code word. And they know that if I'm available, I will send cops to their house based on that code word.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.applies_to: patients in Healthy Start with domestic violence concerns
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Refer patients to Healthy Start by email or chart message; the program is voluntary and confidential.
pearls.verbatim: Just send me an email. He can fill it into their chart and just message me and just be like, hey. I think this person can benefit from your program.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Enrollment in Healthy Start before delivery is ideal; after delivery, support is limited to one-time help if the presenter is available.

pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Breast milk typically does not come in for 3-4 days after delivery; colostrum is sufficient for the newborn's tiny stomach.
pearls.verbatim: their milk's not gonna come in for about three or four days
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: A newborn's stomach is the size of a cherry pit at birth, so the small amount of colostrum is enough.
pearls.verbatim: the stomach is the size of a cherry pit
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: By 10 days, the baby's stomach is about the size of a golf ball to a ping pong ball.
pearls.verbatim: By ten days, it's about a golf ball to a ping ball size
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Hospital formula is chosen by cheapest bid; parents should not assume it is the only or best option for their baby after discharge.

pearls.applies_to: parents of newborns discharged from hospital

pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Similac often causes constipation in breastfed babies who are supplementing with formula.

pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Full-term infants should return to birth weight by 14 days; preterm infants by 21 days.
pearls.verbatim: returning to our birth weight within fourteen days, if they're premature, it's twenty one days.

pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: If a mother is still using a nipple shield at the postpartum visit (after two weeks), that is a red flag; the cause must be investigated.
pearls.verbatim: please tell them if by their postpartum appointment, if they are still using a nipple shield, that's a big no no. We need to figure out why. After two weeks, we should not... No longer need the nipple shield.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: For engorgement, recommend massage, hand expression, and nipple stimulation to help the baby latch.
pearls.verbatim: If they're engorged, it will change the shape, and they're not gonna have anything to attach to. So normally, I just say massage your breast, hand express, nipple stimulation, get your nipples out.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: For PCOS diagnosis, you need two of three: irregular menstrual periods, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, elevated free testosterone. Clinical hirsutism alone does not count.
pearls.verbatim: Three things that you look at currently for polycystic ovary syndrome, irregular menstrual periods, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, elevated pretestosterone. Those are the three things. You have to have two of the three to make the diagnosis.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Jon Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: Primary treatment for PCOS is weight loss.
pearls.verbatim: What's a primary treatment for PCOS? OTPs. Weight loss.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Jon Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: The primary risk of PCOS is endometrial hyperplasia from chronic anovulation; patients need at least two menstrual cycles per year to protect the endometrium.
pearls.verbatim: They don't have to be regular. They have to be one or two a year. Regular cycles is ten years old. It's ten years ago. You need to at least attempt to do this twice a year.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Jon Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: The trend is moving toward treating all patients with insulin resistance with metformin, not just those trying to get pregnant.
pearls.verbatim: And the trend now is is moving more towards treating everybody with insulin resistance and metformin. Used to be you treat with metformin only if you want to get pregnant in more regular periods.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Jon Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: Metformin can lead to pregnancy within 3-4 months in women with PCOS and insulin resistance.
pearls.verbatim: I've had people who are pregnant within three or four months after they start metformin. It was pretty quick.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Jon Calvert
pearls.applies_to: women with PCOS and insulin resistance
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: A CDI query is not a critique of your patient care, it is asking for the language insurance companies require, so respond to it professionally rather than defensively.
pearls.verbatim: That's kind of the initial thought is they're critiquing me and my care. And it's not. It's it's trying to let you know, hey. Here... Here's the game we have to play. Here's the language that has to...
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Peer-to-peer review with insurance company medical directors overturns about 92% of denials, so fighting denials is usually worth the effort.
pearls.verbatim: I would say ninety two percent of the time, we get those overturned.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: hospitals and physicians facing insurance denials
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If a patient improves quickly after switching from observation to inpatient, the insurance company may deny the inpatient stay. If you think they might improve quickly, consider leaving them in observation.
pearls.verbatim: And when we admit them, the clock restarts for inpatient. And there's a lot of times when we do that, and then they get better, and we discharge them the next day or that same day later that day. And then the insurance company is like, what the heck are you guys doing? You know? And so we'll we'll lose that. And if we left them in the observation, we'd have been okay.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: patients being considered for inpatient admission after observation
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If a utilization review nurse says a patient doesn't meet inpatient criteria but you believe they do, it is a documentation issue. The physician advisor can help you describe the severity on paper to justify the inpatient status.
pearls.verbatim: If the utilization review nurse calls you and says this patient doesn't meet criteria for inpatient, and you guys are looking at the patient going, yeah. I really think they do, then it's a documentation issue.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: When a utilization review nurse says the patient doesn't meet inpatient criteria but you believe they do, it's a documentation issue, you need to describe on paper how sick the patient really looks.
pearls.verbatim: I really think they do, then it's a documentation issue.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: clinicians told their patient does not meet inpatient criteria
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Readmissions for post-op complications are bundled with the original surgical stay, making the combined length of stay appear longer.
pearls.verbatim: if it is a post op complication, they will bundle that with the operation. So it's it's bundled. That stay, we're not getting paid for because it's part of what happened before. So that's that's part of the thing with the length of stay is that we... Since they're bundling it with the other one, it now looks like they've been in the hospital for ten days because they... They're additive because of complications.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Medical readmissions, such as for CHF exacerbation, are attributed to the hospital's discharge planning. CMS and insurance companies view a second admission as a patient problem.
pearls.verbatim: if it is something medical, like this is their fourth time getting admitted for exacerbation of CHF, then they blame that on us because we didn't do good discharge planning to keep them out of the hospital.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: When a trauma patient's surgical issues are resolved but they have ongoing medical complications, the surgical team signs off and transfers care to medicine. This allows the medical team to obtain a length of stay extension for the medical issues.
pearls.verbatim: when they come in as a poly or a multi trauma, complicated trauma that needs OR, there's a certain amount of length of time... Length of stay that's allowed with that depending on the surgeries that happen. And so once the surgical part of it is completed, say, you know, six days, and now it's the post op stuff, it's the medical things, it's the, you know, chronic respiratory failure. We can't get them off the vent, those kind of things. That initial stay when the surgeons sign off and flip it over to medicine is because they're not meeting the length of stay requirements from a surgical standpoint. But from a medical standpoint with medical attendings, those kind of complications get us a continued length of stay extension.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: trauma patients with post-surgical medical complications
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Case managers perform an InterQual review every three days to justify continued inpatient stay. The hospital must provide clinicals to the insurance company every 72 hours and a discharge summary upon discharge.
pearls.verbatim: they do every three days that the patient is in. They redo an InterQol for that length of stay to make sure that we're still on... We have to notify that they've been admitted. We have to give them clinicals every seventy two hours, and then we have to send them the discharge summary as soon as that's done. And the insurance company can deny at any point on that timeline.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: UnitedHealthcare allows only 3 days to set up a peer-to-peer review after a denial letter, while most other insurers allow 2 to 4 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: UnitedHealthcare gives us three days to set up a peer to peer once they issue the denial letter. A lot of the other insurance companies, it's two to four weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If you forget to mark an order as 'pending discharge,' the utilization nurse can call the scheduler to get it prioritized.
pearls.verbatim: there's a way to click in there that says pending discharge. Mhmm. And that automatically tells the scheduler that, hey. You need to do this first. But if you've forgotten to do that, the utilization nurses can call up and help you out with that.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: inpatient setting when awaiting discharge-necessary tests or consults
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If a patient does not meet acute criteria, ask the utilization nurse what is missing, often abnormal electrolytes like hypomagnesemia requiring IV magnesium can satisfy invasive criteria.
pearls.verbatim: we finally get extended electrolytes like the mag and the fos and all of that. Hypomagnesemia means you have to give them IV mag. That means criteria for invasion.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: patients whose condition does not meet InterQual acute criteria
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Chronic renal failure patients with stable hyperkalemia (e.g., K+ 5.6) and no EKG changes or symptoms will not meet criteria for acute care.
pearls.verbatim: if you have a chronic renal failure patient that kind of rides high and they're stable, doesn't matter if their potassium is 5.6. If there are no changes on the EKG and they're fine, not gonna meet.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: chronic renal failure patients with asymptomatic hyperkalemia
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: For a UTI under MCG criteria, the patient must have at least one of: hemodynamic instability, changes, obstruction, or pregnancy (though pregnancy is usually easier).
pearls.verbatim: for a UTI, they require at least one of those things. They've gotta be sick. They gotta be hemodynamically unstable. That's one of their things... There's got to be changes and obstruction.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: patients with UTI under private insurance (MCG)
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Elderly men with UTI due to BPH often fail to meet acute criteria because they must be hemodynamically unstable or have obstruction; pregnancy patients usually meet criteria more easily.
pearls.verbatim: your old guys with UTIs because of BPH, that's harder to make. Yeah. They gotta be sick.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.applies_to: elderly men with UTI and BPH
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: The attending physician's note is the final word for coding and insurance; consultant notes are not used unless the attending incorporates them into their own documentation.
pearls.verbatim: Your note is the one that counts. To the insurance company? And to the coders and for everything else. They won't look at the specialist? Why? Because you asked the specialist to come on board. You consulted them. Your word is the final word.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: List up to 46 diagnoses on the discharge summary; including all relevant conditions (e.g., hypokalemia, lymphocytopenia) increases complexity and reduces the insurance company's reason to deny the claim.
pearls.verbatim: It's actually up to 46. Right? Oh, wow. Yeah. When my chart scrubbers and the coders pull it up and look at it, it's a lot. So anything like the lymphocytopenia or, you know, hypokalemia, any of that counts.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: Queries are part of the medical record and are discoverable; do not write snarky responses.
pearls.verbatim: Our queries are part of the medical record. That makes sense. So we can diagnose off of them when you answer the queries, They're part of the medical record and are discoverable. So do not be snarky in those.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If you receive a query from a second-level reviewer or mortality reviewer (e.g., Deborah Attalier or Michelle Voss), answer it immediately; these are critical for hospital metrics.
pearls.verbatim: If you see a query from Deborah Attalier or Michelle Voss, they are our second level reviewers and our mortality reviewers. If you answer none of the other queries that day and push them off to the next day, answer theirs.

pearls.text: Maximum lidocaine dose is 300 mg for adults or 5 mg/kg; know the milligram dose, not milliliters, because 1% = 10 mg/mL and 2% = 20 mg/mL.

pearls.text: Pregnancy centers provide abortion pill reversal services, which will be discussed in a later section.

pearls.text: The 'Pregnancy Decision Guide' is a cognitive tool modeled after the Ottawa decision aid; leave the woman alone with it for a few minutes to help her think through her options away from raw emotion.

pearls.text: Ask the patient her stated intention before the test: 'If your test is positive today, what are your plans for your pregnancy?' This reveals her leaning before any conversation.

pearls.episode_title: Karen Alley on the Hope Pregnancy Center

pearls.text: Avoid 'why' questions because they put the patient on the defensive; instead rephrase as 'What are the reasons...' to keep her open and talking.

pearls.episode_title: Karen Alley on the Hope Pregnancy Center

pearls.text: Do not avoid the hard conversation when a woman says she is not having the baby; take every opportunity to talk it through and remind her of her worth and her baby's value.

pearls.text: Tardive dyskinesia occurs at a rate of 5% per year with first-generation antipsychotics and is often irreversible; catch it early by watching for subtle tongue movements or mouth movements.

pearls.text: Moral injury is defined as committing, participating in, or failing to prevent an act that violates one's deeply held moral values.

pearls.text: Moral injury is strongly associated with betrayal, both betraying someone and being betrayed by a trusted person.

pearls.applies_to: patients with extravasation of pressors such as phenylephrine or levophed
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: During pediatric codes, use an external cognitive aid such as the Braslow tape or the PediStat app ($4, lifetime license) for immediate access to tube sizes, drug doses, and other critical information.
pearls.verbatim: I use an app on my phone called PediStat. It costs me $4. ... it has every tube size, dose, drug.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: IV epinephrine is far more potent than IM: 5 mcg IV produces an effect equivalent to approximately 500 mcg IM.
pearls.verbatim: When you're giving it directly in the IV, like, five mics would have... The equivalent effect of five hundred mics in the muscle.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Engstrom
pearls.applies_to: any patient receiving epinephrine IV vs IM
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Higher-energy X-rays (photons) have a skin-sparing effect, meaning they deposit less energy at the surface and peak deeper, which is advantageous for treating deeper tumors while reducing skin toxicity.
pearls.verbatim: And then the higher energy X rays, they have what we call the skin sparing effect. So that's... Superficially, they don't have a lot of energy. They kinda peek deeper within the patient.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients requiring treatment of deeper tumors
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Proton therapy delivers a low entrance dose, deposits all energy in a Bragg peak that can be targeted to the tumor, and has no exit dose, minimizing radiation to tissues beyond the target.
pearls.verbatim: And, basically, you have a low energy entrance dose, and then it deposits all of its energy in a peak. And we can specify where that peak is based on the energy of the proton. And so we want that peak to be basically within the tumor, and then there's no exit dose beyond that peak.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with tumors near critical structures where sparing beyond the target is crucial
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: IMRT (intensity-modulated radiation therapy) is a complex technique that takes several days to plan and uses many beam angles and shapes to deliver a very conformal dose to the target.
pearls.verbatim: Most of what we do is IMRT or the intensity modulated radiation therapy. It's a really complex plan that takes several days of work to get done. And they basically will have up to an infinite number of beam angles and beam shapes. And so we can get a very, very formal dose to the area that we're trying to treat.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients requiring highly conformal radiation, typically in curative settings
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: After a lumpectomy or brain tumor resection, radiation is almost always given adjuvantly to reduce local recurrence.
pearls.verbatim: We have adjuvant. So after a lumpectomy, after a brain tumor has been resected, we'll always come in with radiation after that. Almost always.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients after lumpectomy for breast cancer or after brain tumor resection
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: In lymphoma, after several cycles of chemotherapy, radiation can be used for consolidation if there are areas not responding to chemotherapy.
pearls.verbatim: And then in the case of lymphoma, after several cycles of chemotherapy, we can consolidate if there's certain areas that aren't responding to chemotherapy.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with lymphoma with residual disease after chemotherapy
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: About 40% of advanced cancer patients receive palliative radiation therapy, and about 40% of a radiation oncologist's daily practice is palliative, focusing on symptom control or prevention with the shortest possible course and least side effects.
pearls.verbatim: Approximately forty percent of advanced cancer patients will get palliative radiation therapy. About forty percent of what we do on a daily basis is palliative radiotherapy.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: advanced cancer patients with symptoms from metastases (e.g., pain, bleeding, obstruction)
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For head and neck cancer, a custom mask immobilizes the head, neck, and shoulders to prevent movement during treatment; if the patient moves, the beam may hit unintended structures.
pearls.verbatim: This is for a head and neck case. So we're able to immobilize the head along with the neck and then the shoulders, ensuring that the patients are not moving while on the treatment table.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients receiving radiation for head and neck cancers
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Multi-leaf collimators (MLCs) made of tungsten shape the radiation beam to conform to the tumor, allowing sparing of organs at risk and reducing toxicity compared to older blocking techniques.
pearls.verbatim: And so this is right at the head of the gantry. These are multi leaf collimators made out of tungsten. So these are very thick, and we're able to shape the beam of radiation to area of interest.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: all patients receiving conformal radiation therapy
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Gamma knife radiosurgery uses a titanium frame fixed to the skull (placed with neurosurgery assistance) to achieve sub-millimeter precision for treating brain lesions, typically in 1-5 fractions.
pearls.verbatim: But we've gotta make sure the patients are immobilized. So this is a titanium frame that we use. The screws don't go through the skull, but they add quite a bit of pressure to the patient's neurosurgery will come in and help us with the placement of this frame.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with brain tumors or arteriovenous malformations requiring stereotactic radiosurgery
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Assess mechanical stability of spinal lesions using the Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS), a six-question tool.
pearls.verbatim: And so for the mechanical, we can use the spinal instability score. It's a six question thing.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: One in five cancer patients will develop a vertebral metastasis at some point.
pearls.verbatim: One in five of all cancer patients will develop a vertebral met at some point.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: In superior vena cava syndrome, intraluminal stenting provides the fastest symptom relief because radiation works slowly via DNA damage.
pearls.verbatim: If you think back to how radiation works, we're looking at DNA damage, so it's not gonna work immediately. So getting, you know, palm involved sometimes doing an intraluminal stenting may help the fastest way.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with superior vena cava syndrome
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For SVC syndrome, if the patient presents with severe symptoms, intraluminal stenting may be the fastest way to relieve obstruction.
pearls.verbatim: So getting, you know, palm involved sometimes doing an intraluminal stenting may help the fastest way.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For SVC syndrome, if tissue diagnosis is not yet available, complete workup with bronchoscopy and sampling before deciding treatment.
pearls.verbatim: And then also looking at what type of cancer it is. So if we don't have a tissue diagnosis, then definitely completing that workup with a bronchoscopy and then sampling that area just so that we know what we're dealing with.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with SVC syndrome without known histology
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For radiosensitive tumors like lymphoma, small cell lung cancer, and germ cell tumors, systemic chemotherapy may work faster than radiation.
pearls.verbatim: Some cancers will respond better to systemic therapy upfront. So lymphomas, small cell lung cancer, germ cell tumors will respond better and faster to chemotherapy.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with lymphoma, small cell lung cancer, or germ cell tumors
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Grade 1 radiation dermatitis: faint erythema, possibly dry itchiness. Grade 2: more intense reaction, moist desquamation. Grade 3: borderline with more confluent moist desquamation.
pearls.verbatim: So grade one is paint erythema, maybe some dry itchiness. These two, I would classify as grade two. And this one might be grade three. It's kinda borderline. This might be a really bad grade two or a grade three reaction, but you see more of this moist desquamation.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For all grades of radiation dermatitis: advise loose clothing and good skin hygiene with mild soap and lukewarm water daily; patients who wash heal faster with less itching.
pearls.verbatim: advise loose clothing, good skin hygiene. So compared to not washing it when... With a mild soap, mild, you know, lukewarm water every day, patients who washed and kept the area clean obviously did better. Less itching, earlier healing times.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Cellulitis over a radiation field is treated just like normal cellulitis; no special coverage is needed.
pearls.verbatim: You treat it just like you would a a normal cellulitis. So so same coverage you would normally do. There's not any specific thing you need to take into account per se when you're empirically covering them.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Gabriel S. Vidal
pearls.applies_to: patients with cellulitis in a previously irradiated area
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: If you suspect a patient may be in danger of self-harm, you should open up the topic and ask questions directly; do not wait for them to bring it up.
pearls.verbatim: If if you ever get the sense that maybe somebody is in danger of self harm, you addressing... You opening up the topic, you asking the questions is probably a really positive thing to do. Don't wait for them to bring it up.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Most suicidal people experience a suicidal episode only once in their lives; if you can stop them during the initial episode, the odds are in your favor that they won't try again.
pearls.verbatim: Most suicidal people experience a suicidal episode only once in their lives. That's a real plus. If you can stop them from killing themselves during the initial epis... Episode, the odds are in your favor that they won't try again later.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: patients in their first suicidal episode
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Suicidal feelings tend to be episodic, like depression; they come and go in waves, so even chronically suicidal people are not suicidal 100% of the time.
pearls.verbatim: Those who have mixed emotions about dying, even chronically suicidal people are not suicidal a 100% of the time. Kinda like people who are chronically depressed. They're not usually in a real depressed state all the time. So it kinda goes like this. Like depression, suicidal feelings tend to be episodic. They come and go in waves.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Burnout prevention should be on the organizational level, not just the individual level; you should have an emotionally healthy place to work.
pearls.verbatim: burnout prevention should be on the organizational level, not just on the individual level. You should have an emotionally healthy place to work.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: A nonanxious presence means staying genuinely calm in circumstances that could potentially lead to anxiety, not just appearing calm while anxiety rages inside.
pearls.verbatim: A nonanxious presence means you're able to stay genuinely calm in circumstances that could potentially lead to anxiety.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: To maintain a nonanxious presence, you must regain control of the thoughts and self-talk that lead to anxiety.
pearls.verbatim: It must… Means you must regain control of the thoughts, self talk, that lead to anxiety.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: The principle of isomorphism: affecting positive change in one area of life can have a generative effect across other areas.
pearls.verbatim: This is known as the principle of isomorphism when you affect change in one area of your life, and it has a generative effect across the board to other areas.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Even while appearing calm, if your anxiety has crossed the optimal level, your cognitive and motor performance will still decrease.
pearls.verbatim: Even while appearing calm, the helper whose anxiety has crossed over the optimal level will still suffer a decrease in cognitive and motor performance.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Self-soothing involves using cognitive, affective, and behavioral skills to create relaxation and lowered reactivity.
pearls.verbatim: Self soothing involves the ability to use cognitive, affective, and behavioral skills to create relaxation and lowered reactivity.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: When a patient is distressed, do not tell them you know how they feel. Instead say 'that must really be awful' and 'I feel your pain with you.'
pearls.verbatim: If we have a nonconscious presence, we can say, that must really be awful. I hear your pain. I feel your pain for you... With you.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: If you let a patient's anger control you (e.g., you start getting really mad), the patient is in control, not you.
pearls.verbatim: If I get in your face and I start calling you names and pointing and stuff and you start getting really, really mad, who's in control? The other person is.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: A non-anxious presence does not deny feelings; it means realizing your position is to minister to and help the patient.
pearls.verbatim: A non anxious is not in any way denying what the feelings are. It's just realizing your position is to be there to minister to them, to help them.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Ask about suicidal thoughts stepwise: start with passive thoughts (I hope I don't wake up), then actively ask if they have a plan, having a plan indicates higher danger.
pearls.verbatim: Thus doesn't mean that person is actively suicidal, but you wanna take it the next step and see if they have a plan. That plan is there. That becomes more dangerous.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: any patient expressing passive death wishes
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Suicide is rarely spontaneous; it is a gradual wearing-away process (suicidal erosion) that can take 10-20 years as the person's ability to cope erodes and they run out of energy.
pearls.verbatim: Suicide is not a spontaneous activity. People do not just wake up one morning and say, well, I think this is a great day to kill myself. Suicide is usually a long term gradual wearing away process called suicidal erosion.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Adolescent suicide can be copycat behavior; after one suicide in a school, others may follow.
pearls.verbatim: And then you get the copycat kind of things where you in the schools. I've been called into several schools along the way because suicide behavior can be very copycat behavior.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: adolescents in school settings after a suicide
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Common themes from suicide notes include: nobody heard me, chronically sick, rejection, feeling that others deserve better, looking for happiness and not finding it, wanting to be with a deceased loved one, and revenge.
pearls.verbatim: Nobody heard me. ... Chronically sick. Rejection from a grandmother. Another rejection. ... Feeling rejected. Rejection. ... Go to be with a deceased loved one. ... there's a revenge factor in it.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: When patients express helplessness, haplessness, and hopelessness, train yourself to listen for clues that suicidal erosion is becoming a strong factor.
pearls.verbatim: when you're talking to patients and they come in and they're expressing helplessness haplessness, and hopelessness of any kind, you have to train yourself to listen to what they're saying.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Never be afraid to ask patients if they have thoughts of hurting themselves or even killing themselves.
pearls.verbatim: never be afraid to ask them if they have thoughts of hurting themselves or even killing themselves.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: any patient with possible suicidal ideation
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Suicide is a form of communication; people who have consistently failed to communicate through normal channels may engage in last-ditch efforts to communicate with the outside world.
pearls.verbatim: People who have consistently failed to communicate effectively through normal challenges or normal challenge... Channels may engage in last resort or last ditch efforts to communicate with the outside world.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Many suicidal gestures are not necessarily intended to die, but are done in the hopes that somebody will grab a clue.
pearls.verbatim: a lot of suicidal gestures, not necessarily intending to die, although some of them do because they're too good at the gesture. They they do a behavior in the hopes that somebody will grab a clue.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: If suicide is a communication technique, ask yourself: what is the person trying to say about his unsatisfied needs?
pearls.verbatim: If suicide is a communication technique, then you must ask yourself, what is the person trying to say? What is the person trying to tell me about his unsatisfied needs?
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Suicide automatically means there are unsatisfied needs.
pearls.verbatim: Suicide automatically means there are unsatisfied needs.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: If suicidal erosion has taken place, the person has probably tried a lot of different things, and none have worked to their satisfaction.
pearls.verbatim: if suicidal erosion has taken place, they've tried... Probably tried a lot of different things. None of them have worked to their satisfaction.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: A suicidal crisis typically lasts only a few minutes; use that window to help the person regain equilibrium and emotional strength before problem-solving.
pearls.verbatim: actively suicidal for a few minutes at most
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: anyone intervening with a suicidal person
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: When a suicidal person says they want to die, they are actually saying they want to be rescued from an intolerable situation.
pearls.verbatim: Remember that when you hear them say they want to die, what they're really saying is they want to be rescued from what they believe is an intolerable situation.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: To identify the significant other in a suicidal patient's life, ask: 'If you were going to write a suicide note, who would you write it to?' or 'Who would be most affected by your suicide?'
pearls.verbatim: Determine the significant other, who that is, you can ask leading questions like, if you were going to write a suicide note, who would you write it to?
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: The relationship between a suicidal person and their significant other is one of dependency; the person believes the other is the only one who can make them happy.
pearls.verbatim: The relationship between the potential suicide and the significant other is one of dependency.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Suicidal individuals often do not have friendships; they 'take hostages' by becoming totally dependent on one person to meet all their needs.
pearls.verbatim: suicidal people don't have friends. They take hostages, where they get totally dependent on one person, or one situation to meet all of their needs, to give them hope, to give them a reason to keep going.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: clinicians assessing social support in suicidal patients
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: A statement like 'You're the only person who understands me' is not a compliment but a confession of poor interpersonal skills and dangerous dependency.
pearls.verbatim: It's not a romantic statement when someone says, you're the only person who understands me.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: clinicians and anyone receiving such statements
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Frustrating or manipulative-seeming behaviors in suicidal patients are manifestations of mental illness, not intentional manipulation; remember this to avoid anger and maintain therapeutic rapport.
pearls.verbatim: it is really important that we are very clear that that is a manifestation of mental illness because then you end up with people like the ER nurse who are angry
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Recognize that acute suicidality differs from chronic suicidal thoughts; many people have passive 'I wish I were dead' thoughts without an emotional charge, and this does not necessarily indicate immediate danger.
pearls.verbatim: Acute suicidality and there's chronic suicidality. There are people who live with this chronic, like, thought in the back of their head that pops up every once in a while that's a... That something wrong go... Something goes wrong, and they say, you know what? It would be a lot better if I just died today. Mhmm. And there's no emotion behind it. It's just a pure thought.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: About 75% of suicidal people will give notice of their intentions in the form of early warning signals; some do so purposely, others inadvertently, with the hope someone will ask them the question and rescue them.
pearls.verbatim: About seventy five percent will give notice of their suicidal intentions in the form of early warning signals. Some will purposely present signals. Others will do so inadvertently.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: general population at risk for suicide
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: A single isolated warning sign does not mean suicide; look for a cluster of several warning signs piling up together, especially in the context of a dramatic life event such as loss, grief, or depression.
pearls.verbatim: But the idea is to look for a cluster of warning signals that start piling up together, especially if it's a... There's a context of something dramatic having happened in the person's life.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Suicidogenic situations, contexts so conducive to suicidal thoughts that the situation itself constitutes a warning signal, include sudden loss of physical function, disfigurement, job loss tied to self-image, divorce, destruction of reputation, or a disfiguring operation.
pearls.verbatim: Examples, a great athlete loses his leg in an accident. Woman proud of her figures told she needs a disfiguring operation. Man gets fired whose self image is wrapped up in his job. Mhmm. Extremely happy marriage ends abruptly. Punch dice. Reputation destruction. Just the situation itself is a warning sign.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: patients experiencing these specific life events
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Behavioral warning signs of suicide include giving away a cherished object in a casual manner; the strongest behavioral warning is a previous suicide attempt.
pearls.verbatim: Giving away a cherished object in a casual manner. Strongest behavioral warning is an attempted suicide, of course.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: 40-50% of completed suicides have made a previous attempt; this history is a critical risk factor.
pearls.verbatim: Forty to fifty percent of completed suicides have tried before.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: patients with a history of suicide attempt
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: 40-50% of completed suicides have tried before.
pearls.verbatim: forty to fifty percent of completed suicides have tried before.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Two years after a suicide gesture is a high-risk period for reattempt.
pearls.verbatim: At the two year mark, it's like, if they're gonna try again, that's when they do it.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Sudden unexplained recovery from severe depression may indicate final problem-solving and increased suicide risk.
pearls.verbatim: Sudden unexplained recovery from a severe depression. ... Too many times people heave a sigh of relief. Oh, they're there. But what all that means is they've done their final problem solving.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: The greatest suicide risk is during the first 90 days after depression begins to lift.
pearls.verbatim: The greatest suicide risk is during the first ninety days after depression begins to lift.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Call 988 (Suicide Prevention Lifeline) before 911 when possible.
pearls.verbatim: Nowadays, they have that 988. Other people are suggesting you call 988 before you call 911.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.applies_to: anyone intervening in a suicide crisis
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Never physically restrain a suicidal person who is armed with a gun or knife.
pearls.verbatim: Never try to physically restrain a suicidal person who is armed with a gun or a knife or anything else like that.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Never leave a suicidal person alone until help arrives.
pearls.verbatim: If you're there in person, never leave a sue... Leave a suicidal person alone until help is there.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Joel S. Leitch

pearls.text: Trafficking does not require monetary exchange; profit can be non-monetary, such as a place to live or rent forgiveness.

pearls.text: For minors under 18, any commercial sex act is automatically human trafficking, regardless of coercion.

pearls.text: Delay in seeking medical care is a red flag because traffickers don't want to lose money by letting victims get care until they are too sick to work.

pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Look for multiple cell phones in the room; victims may have a second phone always connected to the trafficker so someone is always listening to the medical visit.

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.verbatim: it's because she thought if she didn't get better, she could stay there safe. And we... If she did get better, we'd send her home with the guy and let him come see her. So she was just violent.

pearls.applies_to: clinicians caring for suspected trafficking victims
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: When a victim sees the abuser's address on hospital paperwork, explain immediately that the address is only for billing and that the abuser will not be told where they are being sent.

pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.applies_to: During discharge or paperwork encounters with potential trafficking victims
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Recognize that a victim's past negative healthcare experiences, such as being scolded for 'sleeping around', create deep mistrust; counter this by showing nonjudgmental care and addressing their immediate concerns.
pearls.verbatim: I used to think if I could figure out what they were afraid of, that was the biggest hurdle until I met her. And now I think how many bad experiences did they have going to their doctor as a kid and the doctor drunk getting on to them because they were sleeping around.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.applies_to: All healthcare interactions with potential trafficking victims
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Pay for the victim's initial doctor's appointment with grant money while working on getting their insurance coverage sorted.
