pearls.applies_to: Healthcare settings with access to a trafficking grant
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Use available grant funds to cover a victim's first month's rent, plane tickets to family, birth certificates, and food, removing the immediate financial reasons they might return to the trafficker.
pearls.verbatim: The grant covers things like that first deposit on a house to get them someplace safe. I can buy you a plane ticket plus ticket to get you back home to the state where you have family that can protect you. You don't have a birth certificate. Let's go down and buy you and get you a birth certificate. You have no food, so you feel like you're gonna have to go back to this trafficker. Let's do that.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.applies_to: Settings where a federal trafficking grant is available
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: If you can answer any of the key questions (e.g., Does the victim know there are alternatives? What are they threatened with?), you have a good start in gaining their acceptance of help.
pearls.verbatim: If can answer any of those, you got a good start in getting them to accept your help.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.applies_to: Providers assessing readiness to accept assistance
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: There is a my learning module on human trafficking that covers what it looks like and what to look for, which can be used for staff training.
pearls.verbatim: There's a my learning module for human trafficking that goes through a lot of it, what it looks like, what you're looking for.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Connect trafficking survivors with peer support by referring them to community organizations where they can attend events with other survivors who uniquely understand their experiences.
pearls.verbatim: we can refer them to an org community organization where they can they can go to community events with other survivors. And then when things like that happen, they're like, they have... They know who called. They're like, hey. They uniquely understand how they're feeling.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Emergency shelters for trafficking survivors include Spring and Divis; Dragonfly in Oklahoma City provides transitional living; and Rise Above offers a housing grant that pays rent for up to a year.
pearls.verbatim: Emergency shelters will be the spring and Divis. Dragonfly in Oklahoma City does transitional living. We also... Rise Above through the Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse also has a housing grant that we can get some of... We have three clients on it right now. They pay their rent for up to a year and sometimes utilities.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.applies_to: clinicians in Oklahoma needing housing resources for trafficking survivors
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: The documentary 'Buying Her' about demand and pornography, followed by a panel with a survivor and law enforcement, can be used for community education on human trafficking.
pearls.verbatim: We showed a video called Buying Her during Human Trafficking Awareness Month last month, which was all about demand, pornography, and all of that in a community event.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: When involving law enforcement in a trafficking case, call the specialized unit (e.g., TPD metrical unit) directly rather than dispatch to avoid patrol officers who may have previously arrested the victim.
pearls.verbatim: That's also why we call the PLC when they call me, I know if we're gonna need law enforcement, we're not calling dispatch in case they get that patrol officer that's arrested them.
pearls.speaker: Sara Gadd
pearls.applies_to: clinicians coordinating with law enforcement for trafficking cases
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Standard treatment for active TB: 2 months of four-drug therapy (rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) followed by 4-7 months of rifampin and isoniazid.
pearls.verbatim: four drugs to start with for two months or eight weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: For latent TB, treatment is typically 9 months of isoniazid.
pearls.verbatim: I think they get nine months of isoniazid.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Isolate patients with suspected active TB for a minimum of 5 days to 2 weeks until therapy is established and sputum cultures convert to negative.
pearls.verbatim: if you are very highly suspicious, you may wanna isolate them. It says for five days to two weeks until therapy is completed
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: GeneXpert testing is done on sputum samples and can provide drug susceptibility information, including rifampin resistance.
pearls.verbatim: the GeneXpert test is really was what replaced that for us.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Directly observed therapy for TB is done five days per week initially; after the first eight weeks, the frequency may be reduced.
pearls.verbatim: It was five days per week. So... And I I believe that she was not having to do that after the first eight weeks.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.applies_to: patients with active TB on directly observed therapy
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Nonsupervised TB therapy, if used, requires seven days a week dosing: initial phase of all four drugs for at least eight weeks, then continuation phase of rifampin and isoniazid for another four to seven months.
pearls.verbatim: If nonsupervised therapy is is put out there as an option, but once you do that, it's seven days a week. Initial phases of all these four drugs at least eight weeks and then continuation phase of the rifampinin isoniazid for another four to six months.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.applies_to: patients with active TB on nonsupervised therapy
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Extended nine-month TB treatment is indicated for cavitary disease, recurrent TB, and in active smokers.
pearls.verbatim: We often would do six months, but human ingestion, other cases, recurrent TB, months.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.applies_to: patients with cavitary TB, recurrent TB, or who are active smokers
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: BCG vaccine is not used in the US because incidence is low and it does not prevent pulmonary TB, but it reduces TB meningitis and disseminated TB.
pearls.verbatim: The incidence is just not high enough here, and then it's not a hundred percent anyways to prevent. So it doesn't even prevent pulmonary TB is what some of the data shows, so it's just... We definitely still saw it. But it's supposed to decrease the amount of TB meningitis and disseminated TB, so that's why it's still given the BCG.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: In HIV patients with TB, ART should be started only after two weeks of TB therapy have been completed.
pearls.verbatim: That combination of HIV therapy and TB, had to separate from two weeks. So you really couldn't start your a r d s... You know, your your ARTs until you'd have two weeks of TB therapy.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Nucleic acid amplification tests can differentiate between different species of mycobacteria and detect resistance.
pearls.verbatim: thankfully, they are able to do that for us. So that's an advantage of the AFB smears. So we're able to get those numbers... Or get get the actual species there.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Isoniazid can cause hepatotoxicity and peripheral neuropathy; pyridoxine (vitamin B6) is given to prevent neuropathy.
pearls.verbatim: What's the vitamin that we give to try to prevent it? And the eighty six.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Rifampin causes orange-red discoloration of urine; patients should be warned about this.
pearls.verbatim: We always had to warn people that that their urine will change color.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Kyle Jones
pearls.episode_title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO

pearls.text: Do not interrupt the patient while they are telling their story; let them speak without interruption.
pearls.verbatim: And do you interrupt them? No.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: After the patient finishes, ask 'Is there anything else?' to ensure you have the full story.
pearls.verbatim: is there anything else?
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: In acute pancreatitis, antibiotics are indicated only when there is necrotizing pancreatitis involving greater than 30% of the pancreas or a pancreatic abscess.
pearls.verbatim: Greater than 30% of the pancreas has to be necrotizing.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: If there is no necrotizing pancreatitis or abscess, antibiotics are unindicated in acute pancreatitis; no benefit and risks outweigh benefits.
pearls.verbatim: If they don't have that, do not think they have hearts. Wow. Unindicated. No benefit. Risks bigger than benefits.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: patients with acute pancreatitis without necrosis
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: The indication for MRCP in acute pancreatitis is to rule in or out the presence of choledocholithiasis.
pearls.verbatim: rule in or out the presence of choledocholithiasis.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: patients with acute pancreatitis and concern for common bile duct stone
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Concern for choledocholithiasis is raised by a dilated common bile duct on ultrasound and elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase.
pearls.verbatim: Dilated common bile duct and or elevated Billy and elevated alphosphate.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: A HIDA scan is used to detect an obstructing stone in the neck of the gallbladder, not just for bile leak.
pearls.verbatim: If there's a obstructing stone in the neck of it, you can do a HIAS scan to see if there is an obstruction there.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: patients with suspected gallbladder neck obstruction
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: HIDA scan evaluates gallbladder function by giving CCK and measuring ejection fraction; if function is poor, cholecystectomy is indicated.
pearls.verbatim: Alvin Wang is correctly stating that basically the main function of the HIDA scan is to check. You give it CCK. You check how well the gallbladder is functioning. If it's not functioning properly, then you know you've gotta cut it out.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Remember and practice the basics because they are what you will see most commonly in daily practice.
pearls.verbatim: You're gonna see the basics. Okay? You have to remember the basics. You have to practice the basics.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: When you are stuck on management, stop and reopen the differential instead of just acting.
pearls.verbatim: Fix the thing. Stopping. Think and do what? Reopen the differential.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: any clinical situation when management plan is unclear
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Pancreatitis shows inflammatory changes but is not necessarily infectious; antibiotics are not automatically indicated.
pearls.verbatim: Pancreatitis itself does show significant amount of changes, but not necessarily infectious process for necrosis.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: In acute pancreatitis, hyperglycemia worsens because the inflamed pancreas can't keep up insulin production; rising sugars track with worse prognosis.
pearls.verbatim: Pancreas is also related to, like, your insulin. So your pancreas is insulted, and then it just keeps going.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: In acute pancreatitis, a falling calcium (to 6.8) is a red flag for worsening severity, track it along with albumin.
pearls.verbatim: That calcium just keeps dropping, doesn't it? So calcium's down to six eight.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Hypocalcemia in acute pancreatitis is a marker of severity, not a driver of disease; it is a bystander and does not need routine replacement.
pearls.verbatim: the hypocalcemia is a marker of severity. But it is a bystander. It's not a positive problem.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Persistent tachycardia, hypotension, rising WBC/bands, falling bicarbonate, and rising BUN/creatinine despite IVF signal worsening pancreatitis or complications.
pearls.verbatim: resting type of heart is staying, not going away, trouble's coming, WBC and bands are rising.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Always frame orders by stating your clinical concern first: 'I am concerned about X, therefore I will do Y' rather than just ordering a test.
pearls.verbatim: She did not say get a chest X-ray. She said, I'm concerned about X. I will therefore do Y.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Each patient is an n-of-1; having 20 other patients is never an excuse for missing deterioration in a critically ill patient.
pearls.verbatim: Every person is an n of one.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Serial assessment of mental status, respiratory rate, oxygen requirement, and volume status is critical in pancreatitis; encephalopathy is a definite change that warrants immediate attention.
pearls.verbatim: She is now getting encephalopathy. This is a definite change from a few hours ago.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: Gadolinium contrast does not cause renal failure like CT contrast does; it is more harmful if you already have renal failure, especially when GFR is 30 and below.
pearls.verbatim: The gadolinium is more bad if you have renal failure. I don't think it causes like, that like CT contrast. 30 and below. That's when it's really bad.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: When consultants disagree on fluid management, reassess the patient yourself and facilitate a conference call between services.
pearls.verbatim: I will need to reassess the patient. Good. I'll need to reassess the patient. That's a good answer.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: attending caught between conflicting specialist recommendations
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: When pulmonary wants fluids and renal wants diuresis, gather information to reassess volume status and discuss with both specialists to align goals.
pearls.verbatim: Alright. So correct answers include gather information to reassess volume status. K? And discuss with your specialist.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee

pearls.text: In a patient who is hypervolemic but intravascularly depleted, doing nothing is an action; no immediate change to fluids may be correct.
pearls.verbatim: No action is an action. Do you understand this? By doing nothing, you are doing something.
pearls.speaker: Dr. Lawrence Lee
pearls.applies_to: patients with third spacing and hypoperfusion
pearls.episode_title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee
